newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore financial services sector grows 6.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Singapore financial services sector grows 6.2 pct.

text.p: Singapore's financial services sector grew by 6.2 percent in 1996, up from the 5.4 percent growth seen in 1995, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said in its 1996/97 annual report on Tuesday.
The MAS, Singapore's central bank, said the better performance was due mainly to strong growth in foreign exchange trading and continued expansion of the Asian dollar market.

The average daily trading volume of foreign exchange increased in 1996 by 17.7 percent to US$128.6 billion, while trading on the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) declined by seven percent to 87,859 lots.
Turnover on the Singapore stock exchange fell by 8.7 percent to S$88.9 billion.
Total assets in the Asian dollar market rose by 6.0 perent to US$506.9 billion. Total assets in the domestic banking units of banks grew by 12.5 percent to S$252.7 billion.
During the first quarter of 1997 foreign exchange activity surged to US$187.7 billion per day while the financial services sector as a whole grew by 13.5 percent.

Total assets in the Asian dollar market grew by 11.6 perent on a year-on-year basis to US$534.3 as at the end of March this year, while total assets in the domestic banking units of banks rose 13.7 percent year-on-year to $265.9 billion.
Turnover on SIMEX moderated to 85,400 lots per day in the first quarter but turnover on the Singapore stock exchange rose to S$33.0 billion compared with S$31.7 billion in the same quarter of 1996.
